main_body: Flat-roofed desert house, 64x64 px. A big terrace roof seen from above (tan floor with a parapet rim, a rug and a roof hatch) sits over a south wall with an arched door and a lattice window.
top_band: Roof terrace L≈175 (#d9a478) with a lighter #ebc39b parapet rim at the top, rows 1-29 in the x=32 column. A light front-edge line at row 28-30 closes it.
evidence: The column scan at x=32 shows the roof floor (rows 4-29, with a light rim at 1-3 and a front edge at 28-30), then a dark eave/edge row 32-33 (#8f5038, #69392b). The wall face follows from row 34 downward at L≈122, a clear step of more than 50 L. The roof carries horizontal-surface props (a rug with fringe, a hatch with a ladder), so it reads as a surface seen from above, not a wall panel. The roof is large rather than strongly foreshortened, but it is clearly a separate top band above a vertical door-and-window face. The door has a white arch frame and the window has a dark lattice interior and a sill, which gives some inset. This is a legitimate flat-roof 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral dark edge pixels), which fits the standard. Texture is limited to sparse dither speckle on the roof and wall. The candidate is thinner than the references: 27 distinct colours against 66 and 185, and 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18. It also has 11% flat-fill coverage (the rug, the door and parts of the wall) where both references have 0%. The wall has only about 3 tones, the roof about 4, and there are no tile scallops or per-stone shading. Next to the references it looks flatter and simpler.
